setting.antispam.captcha_mode.descriptio: Off, or a question you set. Swapping in a hosted captcha is a small amount of code against the provider seam, not a setting — see the plugin and anti-spam documentation.
setting.antispam.captcha_mode.label: Registration challenge
setting.antispam.honeypot.description: Adds a field a person never sees and a bot fills in. Costs a real visitor nothing, and catches the least sophisticated half of them.
setting.antispam.honeypot.label: Hidden-field trap
setting.antispam.login_ip_attempts.descr: The per-account counters catch somebody guessing at one account. This one catches the opposite shape — a single guess against each of a thousand accounts — and shares the lockout window with them. 0 disables it.
setting.antispam.login_ip_attempts.label: Failed logins from one address before lockout
setting.antispam.message_per_hour.descri: Counted per sender, not per recipient — one message to ten people is one send and ten deliveries.
setting.antispam.message_per_hour.label: Private messages per hour
setting.antispam.min_form_seconds.descri: A form submitted faster than this is treated as automated. 0 disables the check. Keep it low — a password manager filling a form in two seconds is a real person.
setting.antispam.min_form_seconds.label: Minimum seconds to fill the registration form
setting.antispam.moderate_first_posts.de: Posts are held for approval until the account has this many. 0 disables it. The cheapest control a board has: spam accounts post once and never return.
setting.antispam.moderate_first_posts.la: Hold a new member’s first posts
setting.antispam.post_per_hour.descripti: Threads and replies together. 0 disables the limit. Members with “bypass flood check” are exempt, as they are from the flood interval.
setting.antispam.post_per_hour.label: Posts per hour
setting.antispam.register_ip_per_hour.de: Counted per /24 (or /48), so a household or an office shares one allowance. Independent of the challenge: a board with no captcha is the one that needs this most. 0 disables the limit.
setting.antispam.register_ip_per_hour.la: Registrations per hour from one address
setting.antispam.report_per_hour.descrip: A limit on reporting is a limit on asking for help, so set it high enough that a member having a bad day is not silenced. 0 disables.
setting.antispam.report_per_hour.label: Reports per hour
setting.antispam.reset_ip_per_hour.descr: The same limit counted per requesting /24, which is what stops one caller working through a list of e-mail addresses. 0 disables it.
setting.antispam.reset_ip_per_hour.label: Password reset requests per hour from one address
setting.antispam.reset_per_hour.descript: How many reset mails one e-mail address can be sent in an hour. Without it, the reset form is an e-mail cannon anybody can point at anybody. 0 disables the limit.
setting.antispam.reset_per_hour.label: Password reset requests per hour per address
setting.antispam.search_per_hour.descrip: Searching is the most expensive thing a guest can do. 0 disables.
setting.antispam.search_per_hour.label: Searches per hour
setting.antispam.upload_per_hour.descrip: Attachments and avatars. 0 disables the limit.
setting.antispam.upload_per_hour.label: Uploads per hour
setting.board.description.description: Used as the default meta description for the board index.
setting.board.description.label: Board description
setting.board.legacy_redirects.descripti: Answer MyBB addresses — showthread.php, forumdisplay.php, member.php, index.php, and the rewritten Thread-Title-91, Thread-Title--4102 and Forum-Name-3 forms — with a permanent redirect (308) to the imported content. Needs an import: the redirect is a lookup in the legacy id map.
setting.board.legacy_redirects.label: Redirect old MyBB URLs
setting.board.logo_alt.description: What a screen reader announces in place of the logo. Leave empty to use the board name, which is usually what the logo says anyway.
setting.board.logo_alt.label: Logo alt text
setting.board.logo_dark.description: Used when the reader is in dark mode. Falls back to the light one.
setting.board.logo_dark.label: Logo (dark)
setting.board.logo_light.description: Shown in the header in place of the board name. Uploaded, not typed.
setting.board.logo_light.label: Logo (light)
setting.board.name.description: Shown in the header, page titles, and outgoing e-mail.
setting.board.name.label: Board name
setting.board.offline.description: Closes every board page to everyone without the "can view board offline" permission: they get the offline message instead, and the board’s feeds answer 503. Administrators keep access so they can finish maintenance, and the login screen, the control panel and the health endpoint stay reachable. An offline board is never indexable.
setting.board.offline.label: Board offline
setting.board.offline_message.descriptio: Shown on the offline page, and returned as the body of the 503 the feeds answer with. Left empty, a plain maintenance line is shown instead.
setting.board.offline_message.label: Offline message
setting.board.url.description: The absolute public origin, with no trailing slash — https://forum.example. Every link the board sends is built from it, because nothing in a queued job or a mail template knows the request that caused it. Left empty, mail still arrives and carries no link. Setting APP_URL in the environment overrides this and makes the box below inert.
setting.board.url.label: Board address
setting.display.default_locale.descripti: The language a page is written in when the reader has expressed no preference — a BCP-47 tag such as en, de or pt-BR. A signed-in member overrides it in their control panel, and a visitor who has not is served whichever language their browser asks for that this board has a catalog for. Left at a language nothing translates, every message falls back to English rather than disappearing.
setting.display.default_locale.label: Default language
setting.display.posts_per_page.descripti: Capped to protect the thread-view query budget.
setting.display.posts_per_page.label: Posts per page
setting.display.threads_per_page.descrip: Capped to protect the forum-display query budget.
setting.display.threads_per_page.label: Threads per page
setting.federation.github_client_id.desc: From the OAuth app you registered with GitHub.
Stored as written and never shown again. Leave the box empty to keep the secret already saved.
setting.federation.github_enabled.descri: Off by default, and off is a position: turning it on means GitHub is told the address of this board every time somebody signs in with it, and gets to see who your members are. Needs the client ID and secret below, from a GitHub OAuth app whose callback URL is your board address followed by /auth/sso/github/callback.
setting.federation.github_enabled.label: Sign in with GitHub
setting.federation.google_client_id.desc: From the OAuth 2.0 client you created in the Google Cloud console.
Stored as written and never shown again. Leave the box empty to keep the secret already saved.
setting.federation.google_enabled.descri: Off by default. Turning it on means Google meets your members: it learns this board’s address and who signs in with it. The callback URL to give Google is your board address followed by /auth/sso/google/callback.
setting.federation.google_enabled.label: Sign in with Google
setting.federation.link_from_usercp.desc: On, a member manages their linked providers and passkeys from /usercp/security. Off, existing links keep working and the page stops offering to change them — for a board where identity is decided by the organisation and not by the member.
setting.federation.link_from_usercp.labe: Let members link and unlink their own sign-ins
setting.federation.oidc_client_id.descri: The client this board is registered as with that provider.
setting.federation.oidc_client_id.label: OpenID client ID
setting.federation.oidc_client_secret.de: Stored as written and never shown again. Leave the box empty to keep the secret already saved.
setting.federation.oidc_enabled.descript: The generic path, and the one an organisation usually wants: any provider that publishes an OpenID Connect discovery document — Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak, Authentik, your own. Off by default. The callback URL is your board address followed by /auth/sso/oidc/callback.
setting.federation.oidc_enabled.label: Sign in with your own OpenID provider
setting.federation.oidc_issuer.descripti: The issuer, with no trailing slash and no path of its own — the board asks it for /.well-known/openid-configuration and reads every endpoint from there, so nothing else needs configuring.
setting.federation.oidc_issuer.label: Issuer URL
setting.federation.oidc_label.descriptio: The button reads “Continue with …” and this fills the gap. Left empty it says “Single sign-on”, which tells a member nothing about which login they are being sent to.
setting.federation.oidc_label.label: What to call it on the sign-in page
setting.federation.oidc_scopes.descripti: Space-separated. `openid` is always sent whether or not it is here. The default asks for the address and the display name, which is the least this board can register an account from.
setting.federation.oidc_scopes.label: Scopes to ask for
setting.federation.passkeys_enabled.desc: Lets a member add a passkey from their account security page and sign in with it afterwards — a fingerprint, a face, or a security key, with no password to phish. Nothing leaves this board: the passkey is created against your own address and no third party is involved. A member who has one keeps their password unless they clear it themselves.
setting.legal.privacy.description: Markdown, published at /privacy and linked from the footer. Emptied, the page and the link go. It ships as a template describing what this software does by default — your host, your mail provider and anything you have added are yours to describe.
setting.legal.privacy.label: Privacy policy
setting.legal.terms.description: Markdown, published at /terms and linked from the footer. Registration asks the visitor to accept it before the account is created, so emptying this box takes the page, the footer link and the checkbox away together. What ships is a template written to be replaced: read it, make it say what your community actually does, and take advice on it if it matters.
setting.legal.terms.label: Terms of service
setting.mail.from.description: The address every message comes from. It must be on a domain the provider has verified — a sender the provider does not recognise is rejected outright, and the rejection is not retried because it would fail identically every time.
setting.mail.from.label: Sender address
setting.mail.from_name.description: Display name shown beside the sender address. Empty sends the bare address.
setting.mail.from_name.label: Sender name
setting.mail.http_endpoint.description: Only for the provider-API transport. The board posts Resend’s exact field names with a Bearer token, so this works for Resend and for anything that copies it — and not for Postmark or Mailgun, whose SMTP hosts are the way in.
setting.mail.http_endpoint.label: Provider API endpoint
setting.mail.http_token.description: Only for the provider-API transport. Stored on the board.
setting.mail.http_token.label: Provider API key
setting.mail.smtp_host.description: Only for the SMTP transport. For example smtp.resend.com.
setting.mail.smtp_host.label: SMTP host
setting.mail.smtp_password.description: Use an app password rather than the password you sign in with, wherever the provider offers one. Stored on the board.
setting.mail.smtp_password.label: SMTP password
setting.mail.smtp_port.description: 465 for implicit TLS, 587 for STARTTLS. Picking the security mode below that does not match the port is the usual cause of a connection that hangs rather than failing.
setting.mail.smtp_port.label: SMTP port
setting.mail.smtp_security.description: Implicit TLS encrypts the socket before the first byte (port 465). STARTTLS connects in the clear and upgrades, and the board refuses to continue if the upgrade fails (port 587). "None" is genuinely unencrypted and is for a relay on this machine and nothing else.
setting.mail.smtp_security.label: SMTP security
setting.mail.smtp_username.description: Empty only for a relay that does not authenticate. Resend wants the literal word “resend” here, with the API key as the password.
setting.mail.smtp_username.label: SMTP username
setting.mail.transport.description: A provider’s JSON API, an SMTP server, or nothing at all. "Not sending" writes each message to the server log and delivers none of them — which is the right default for a board nobody has configured yet, and a broken board the moment registration asks anybody to confirm an address.
setting.mail.transport.label: How mail is sent
setting.posting.edit_grace_seconds.descr: Seconds after posting during which an author fixing their own post leaves no "edited by" notice on it. 0 always shows the notice. A moderator editing somebody else's post is never silent, however soon it happens, and the revision history records every edit either way — this hides the line under the post, nothing else.
setting.posting.edit_grace_seconds.label: Silent edit window
setting.posting.flood_seconds.descriptio: Minimum seconds between posts by one user. 0 disables the check. Users with "bypass flood check" are exempt.
setting.posting.flood_seconds.label: Post flood interval
setting.posting.max_length.description: Characters of source text, before rendering.
setting.posting.max_length.label: Maximum post length
setting.posting.thread_ratings_enabled.d: Members with permission can give each thread one 1–5 rating.
setting.registration.enabled.description: Off closes the board to new members: the Register link goes, /register says so instead of offering a form, and the action behind it refuses a submission sent straight to it. Existing members sign in as before, the installer still creates the first administrator, and "community user:create" still works — closing the door is not the same as locking yourself out.
setting.registration.enabled.label: Allow new registrations
setting.registration.method.description: "none" logs the user straight in. "email" requires a link. "admin" queues the account for manual approval. "both" requires e-mail then admin.
setting.registration.method.label: Activation method
setting.registration.min_password_length: Applied to new passwords only. Raising it does not invalidate existing ones — those are rehashed on next login.
setting.registration.username_max.descri: Must not exceed the 64-character database column.
setting.registration.username_max.label: Maximum username length
setting.registration.username_min.descri: Counted in Unicode code points, not bytes.
setting.registration.username_min.label: Minimum username length
setting.reputation.allow_negative.descri: Members can rate somebody down as well as up. Off makes reputation a thanks button, which is what most boards actually want — and takes the Rate link off posts, since the Thanks button on each one is then the whole of what the rating form could offer.
setting.reputation.allow_negative.label: Allow negative ratings
setting.reputation.comment_required.desc: A rating must say why. A number with no reason attached is the part of reputation people argue about — but it also removes the one-press Thanks button from posts, because one press cannot carry a reason. Off by default: thanking an answer that helped should be a single click, and it is negative ratings that need explaining.
setting.reputation.enabled.description: Members can rate each other. Off hides every control and every total; existing ratings are kept, so switching it back on restores them.
setting.reputation.enabled.label: Reputation enabled
setting.reputation.min_posts_to_give.des: A brand-new account cannot rate anybody until it has posted this many times. 0 disables the requirement.
setting.search.enabled.description: Off takes the Search link out of the board navigation, replaces /search and any results page still linked to with a line saying so, and answers GET /api/v1/search with a 403. The index is kept and goes on being maintained, so switching it back on needs no reindex.
setting.search.enabled.label: Enable search
setting.search.flood_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between searches per user. Replaces the per-group searchfloodtime permission, which could not obey the numeric combination rule — see docs/mybb-parity.md.
setting.search.flood_seconds.label: Search flood interval
setting.search.min_word_length.descripti: A search is refused unless at least one of its words is this long, so at 3 "a good post" runs and "a b c" does not. The short words are not dropped — they are still sent to the index, which drops the ones carrying no meaning on its own. Raise it if short words are what your expensive searches turn out to be.
setting.search.min_word_length.label: Shortest word a search may rest on
setting.security.lockout_minutes.descrip: How long an account stays locked after too many failures. The window the counts above are measured over, and the one the per-address limit on the anti-spam screen shares.
setting.security.lockout_minutes.label: Lockout duration (minutes)
setting.security.max_account_login_attem: The same count for one account across every address at once, which is what a guess spread over a botnet meets. Keep it well above the per-address number — it locks the real owner out too, which is the cost of it working at all. 0 disables it.
Failed login attempts before an account locks everywhere
setting.security.max_login_attempts.desc: Counted per account per address, so somebody guessing at one account from one place meets this first. 0 disables it.
setting.security.session_idle_days.descr: How long a sign-in lasts, counted from the moment it happened and not extended by use — a session in daily use still ends on its date. Separate from “keep me signed in”, which is a different token with a longer life of its own and does renew as it is used.
setting.security.session_idle_days.label: Session lifetime (days)
setting.security.two_factor_enabled.desc: Lets a member add an authenticator app to their account from /usercp/security, and asks for a code after their password from then on. Needs AUTH_SECRET set, because the secret the app holds is sealed with a key derived from it.
setting.security.two_factor_required_for: An account that can open the control panel is asked to set up an authenticator app before it can be used, and cannot turn it off again while it holds that access. The control panel can rewrite the whole board, so a password on its own is a thin thing to protect it with.
Require it of anyone who can reach the control panel
sso.approval: Your account has been created. An administrator reviews new members here, so you cannot sign in until that has happened.
sso.conflict: An account here already claims that identity. Sign in the way you did before and manage the link from your account security page.
sso.expired: That sign-in attempt had expired by the time it came back, so nothing was done. Start it again from this page.
sso.failed: That sign-in did not complete. Nothing changed here, so it is safe to retry.
sso.forbidden: That sign-in cannot open an account here. If you already have one, sign in with your password and link the two from your account security page.
sso.invalid: The provider did not send enough to open an account with — a confirmed e-mail address, at least. Register with a password instead.
sso.linked: That sign-in is now linked to your account.
sso.off: That way of signing in is not switched on for this board.
sso.refused: The sign-in was cancelled, so nothing changed here.
sso.slowdown: Too many accounts have been opened from your connection. Try again later.
sso.unlinked: That sign-in has been unlinked. It can no longer reach your account.
subscription.doneOne: Done — you will not be notified about that any more.
subscription.emailsOff: Done — subscription e-mails are off. Your subscriptions are unchanged, and you will still see them in your notifications.
subscription.stopped: You will not be notified about that any more.

themeToken.accent-foreground.label: Text on the hover surface
themeToken.accent.hint: The tint behind a hovered row or menu item.

themeToken.group.brand.blurb: The accent, and the four things it marks: the one primary button, the current item in a list, a link’s underline and the focus outline. The rest of the palette holds no hue at all, so these four are the whole of making the board yours. Set them together — a green button with a grey focus ring looks like a board that was half rebranded.
themeToken.group.brand.title: Brand
themeToken.group.destructive-actions.blu: Delete, ban, and anything else that cannot be taken back.
themeToken.group.forums-and-threads.blur: These carry meaning rather than decoration — a locked thread is not merely a different colour — so every state a hue marks is also a word in the page. Changing them is safe; removing the difference between them is not.
